1. Discotrade misses journal reminders ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>Runner.run() records the new journal preface in the running job but still writes job.prompt,
>without the preface, to Claude. When a discotrade builder answer or CLI send starts while
>meta/journal.md is dirty, the builder misses the instruction to commit it before continuing the
>mission, despite the job record saying that instruction was delivered.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/runner.py[R653-656]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/5/files#diff-33639dfe2ec751f3319053b79320b1fb736bb2a8eac7a7082ae582f76782cf54R653-R656) > >```diff >+ started: dict[str, Any] = {"head_at_start": head_at_start} >+ if preface is not None: >+ started["prompt"] = f"{preface}\n\n{current.prompt}" >+ job = self.spool.transition(current, "running", **started) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The daemon supplies the preface at dispatch and the runner records it, but the subprocess receives
>the unprefaced prompt. Discotrade's builder workflow requires its journal to be updated as units
>proceed.
>
> > [hands -> discotrade](https://app.qodo.ai/management/relationships?repoId=77e6b9e3-9009-4fbe-bd8c-e1c4bd92a98f&relatedRepoId=f8bc154f-fef0-4515-a253-775ba818fa12&view=table) > [src/hands/daemon.py\[665-671\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/daemon.py/#L665-L671) > [src/hands/runner.py\[617-618\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/runner.py/#L617-L618) > [src/hands/runner.py\[653-656\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/runner.py/#L653-L656) > [src/hands/runner.py\[693-701\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/runner.py/#L693-L701) > [External repo: SigorMatt/discotrade, meta/BUILDER-17-PROMPT.md \[64-74\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/discotrade/blob/ca91ecf29237f84a114fa5d31e5f23478badfa87/meta/BUILDER-17-PROMPT.md/#L64-L74) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The running job records a journal preface that Claude never receives. This defeats the dirty-journal reminder for discotrade builder sessions. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/runner.py[617-618] >- src/hands/runner.py[653-656] >- src/hands/runner.py[693-701] > >## Recommended Fix >Pass the same prefaced prompt to `_write_prompt` that the running job records, and test the subprocess input as well as the job record. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. Doctor fails on unreadable worktree data ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>_worktrees_check calls admin.iterdir() without handling filesystem errors, although it handles
>unreadable individual worktree records. If a role clone’s worktree directory is unreadable or
>disappears during the check, hands doctor exits with a generic error instead of reporting its
>other checks.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/doctor.py[1837]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/5/files#diff-3910c7af1fd466f413148b4c6d7df4a5256ce2fe25441aa2ebb485a058b52f18R1837-R1837) > >```diff >+ entries = sorted(admin.iterdir()) if admin.is_dir() else [] >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new check runs as part of every doctor report, but only reads of individual gitdir files catch
>OSError; the CLI handles an escaping OSError as a top-level failure.
>
> > [src/hands/doctor.py\[223-229\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/doctor.py/#L223-L229) > [src/hands/doctor.py\[1833-1848\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/doctor.py/#L1833-L1848) > [src/hands/cli.py\[960-962\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/cli.py/#L960-L962) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >### Issue description >A filesystem error while listing worktree records aborts the entire doctor report. >### Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/doctor.py[1833-1848] >### Recommended Fix >Catch directory-listing errors and represent the unreadable clone as a worktrees check result, allowing the remaining doctor checks to run. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
3. A restarted kickoff no longer resets the consult count ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>wants_journal_sentence leaves out kickoffs only through the in-memory Daemon.kickoffs set. When
>a hands go job (origin cli) is still held or queued across a daemon restart and the journal is
>dirty, the runner rewrites the stored prompt to <sentence>\n\n<kickoff>. consults_used
>recognises a kickoff by record.prompt.strip() in kickoffs, so that job no longer resets the
>consultation count, and the pipeline can stop early on max_consults.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/daemon.py[R715-719]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/5/files#diff-2224a4a9fb4a4b1dff488eefd97ff2528609544c0e2c33da2ddf160312fb97d6R715-R719) > >```diff >+ return ( >+ job.role == "builder" >+ and (job.origin == "cli" or is_builder_answer(job)) >+ and job.id not in self.kickoffs >+ ) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>kickoffs lives only in memory (daemon.py 192-196), and its comment admits a carried-over `hands
>go gets the sentence. The runner persists the prefaced prompt into the record at the running`
>transition (runner.py 653-656). PlaybookEngine.consults_used matches kickoff jobs by exact prompt
>text (playbook.py 2585-2589). Before this PR, kickoffs used go_builder and never got a reminder,
>so their prompt always matched.
>
> > [src/hands/daemon.py\[189-197\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/daemon.py/#L189-L197) > [src/hands/runner.py\[650-656\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/runner.py/#L650-L656) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2579-2590\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2579-L2590) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A kickoff is recognised only through an in-memory set, so after a restart it gets the journal sentence. That rewrites its recorded prompt, and consults_used stops treating it as a kickoff. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/daemon.py[711-719] >- src/hands/api.py[375-379] > >## Recommended Fix >Decide kickoff status from persisted data. Either compare `job.prompt.strip()` with the playbook's kickoff values (`PipelineState.kickoffs` plus the loaded book's), or store a marker on the job record at enqueue, and check that in `wants_journal_sentence` instead of `self.kickoffs`. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
4. Old spool state is skipped after migration ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>The new-machine procedure extracts the archive and proceeds to daemon startup without running `hands
>migrate-spool` for the flat spool layout that this runbook also describes. When the archived state
>predates per-project spools, the daemon reads the new per-project directory instead of the restored
>jobs, roles, inbox and pipeline files.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/OPERATIONS.md[317]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/5/files#diff-3b441db82a6aa05a4005032fb6541cc4719b4ef8308cb78ddcfcb80a6da0bf91R317-R317) > >```diff >+6. `tar -C ~ -xzpf ~/hands-move.tgz`; `stat -c '%a %n' ~/.hands/*.toml >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The runbook acknowledges the old flat layout, while daemon construction uses the configured
>per-project spool root and the separate migration command performs the required move.
>
> > [docs/OPERATIONS.md\[77-78\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/docs/OPERATIONS.md/#L77-L78) > [docs/OPERATIONS.md\[315-329\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/docs/OPERATIONS.md/#L315-L329) > [src/hands/config.py\[451-454\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/config.py/#L451-L454) > [src/hands/spool.py\[867-889\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/spool.py/#L867-L889) > [src/hands/daemon.py\[127-133\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/daemon.py/#L127-L133) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >### Issue description >The restore procedure does not move archived flat spool state into the project's spool before starting the daemon. >### Fix Focus Areas >- docs/OPERATIONS.md[315-329] >### Recommended Fix >Add a conditional step for a restored pre-per-project spool: run the documented spool migration and reconcile its destination with the configured project name before starting the daemon. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

5. Sub-agents alter protected metadata 📘 Rule violation § Compliance
>
>Description >
> >
>meta/plan.md and meta/CHECKPOINT.md are changed in the U0 plan unit even though the mission's
>standing constraint forbids sub-agents from editing them. The protected metadata therefore has a
>sub-agent-authored change in this PR, contrary to the repository workflow requirement.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[meta/plan.md[R13-15]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/5/files#diff-7b1c6ea9ab4fd6179a8304348a94fbf1fa61cfb6aafed7ec549bcd7b7f8df461R13-R15) > >```diff >+- [x] U0 Plan, branch and findings (`plan:`) (this commit) — this file, >+ meta/CHECKPOINT.md, meta/journal.md, meta/findings/FINDINGS.md >+ (H-062..H-069 filed; H-064, H-065 decided; H-061 decided; H-051 Status corrected) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The changed plan records U0 as modifying both protected metadata files, while the changed checkpoint
>explicitly states that sub-agents do not edit meta/plan.md or meta/CHECKPOINT.md. This conflicts
>with the checklist's prohibition on sub-agent changes to either file.
>
> > Rule 3263089: [Sub-agents must not modify plan/checkpoint metadata files](https://app.qodo.ai/rules/3263089?state=active) > [meta/plan.md\[13-15\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/meta/plan.md/#L13-L15) > [meta/CHECKPOINT.md\[39-41\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/meta/CHECKPOINT.md/#L39-L41) >
>

Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The PR changes `meta/plan.md` and `meta/CHECKPOINT.md` in the unit governed by the standing rule that sub-agents must not edit those files. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- meta/plan.md[13-15] >- meta/CHECKPOINT.md[3-10] > >## Recommended Fix >Remove sub-agent-authored edits to `meta/plan.md` and `meta/CHECKPOINT.md` from the sub-agent unit commit, and have the orchestrator or authorized maintainer apply any required plan and checkpoint updates separately. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

6. Quota capture can abort and leave an empty file ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>The script cuts transcript, stream-json, grep and inbox lines with cut -c1-4000, then pipes
>everything into a Python redactor that calls sys.stdin.read() in text mode. GNU cut -c counts
>bytes, so a long line whose 4000th byte falls inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character (—, § and
>similar are common in this project's transcripts) is split mid-character; under a UTF-8 locale stdin
>decodes strictly, the redactor raises UnicodeDecodeError, and the capture fails, leaving only the
>empty $out that noclobber already created.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh[R216-218]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/5/files#diff-8aaeceeb41390e763bbf25d16de0f7662c3cd93c4286e286af0ece466fe82359R216-R218) > >```diff >+text = sys.stdin.read() >+for form in sorted(forms, key=len, reverse=True): >+ text = text.replace(form, "[redacted]") >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Lines 101, 107-108, 125 and 139 pipe through cut -c1-"$CUT", and GNU coreutils treats -c the
>same as -b (bytes). Line 216 reads stdin as strict UTF-8, and line 225 redirects with noclobber,
>so the output file exists before Python fails. The script then prints 'writing … failed' and exits
>1. Node writes transcript JSON with non-ASCII characters left as raw UTF-8, and those lines are
>often far longer than 4000 bytes, so a cut landing inside a character is likely.
>
> > [scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh\[98-142\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh/#L98-L142) > [scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh\[216-229\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh/#L216-L229) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The redactor reads stdin as strict UTF-8, but `cut -c` truncates by bytes and can split a multi-byte character. When that happens the whole capture fails and leaves an empty output file. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh[216-216] > >## Recommended Fix >Replace `text = sys.stdin.read()` with `text = sys.stdin.buffer.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")`, and write the result with `sys.stdout.buffer.write(text.encode("utf-8"))` or keep `sys.stdout.write` with UTF-8 output. Optionally delete `$out` when the pipeline fails. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
7. Restored held jobs block the kickoff step ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>The migration procedure instructs the operator to run hands go after startup without first
>resolving any restored builder jobs. When the restored spool contains a held builder apply—the
>condition the preceding step says the start notification can announce—Api.kickoff refuses the
>command because the builder is busy.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[docs/OPERATIONS.md[331]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/5/files#diff-3b441db82a6aa05a4005032fb6541cc4719b4ef8308cb78ddcfcb80a6da0bf91R331-R331) > >```diff >+ sessions stayed behind. >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The instructions say startup can republish held jobs, then direct an unconditional kickoff; the
>kickoff path expressly refuses while any builder job is held, queued or running.
>
> > [docs/OPERATIONS.md\[325-331\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/docs/OPERATIONS.md/#L325-L331) > [src/hands/api.py\[478-500\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/api.py/#L478-L500) > [src/hands/api.py\[502-515\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/api.py/#L502-L515) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >### Issue description >The migration runbook calls for a kickoff even when a restored held builder job makes kickoff impossible. >### Fix Focus Areas >- docs/OPERATIONS.md[325-331] >### Recommended Fix >Tell operators to inspect and resolve restored held or queued builder jobs before using `hands go`, and describe when a fresh kickoff is appropriate. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
8. Kits over about 9.4 MiB can't be applied from the laptop ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>apply_run accepts zips up to [files] kit_max_mb (20 MiB by default) and base64-encodes the
>entire kit into one socket request, while call checks that request against the daemon’s 12.5 MiB
>LINE_LIMIT. A zip above roughly 9.4 MiB can therefore pass the kit-size check but be refused
>before reaching the daemon with an “over the daemon’s line room” message, even though the phone’s
>kit path accepts the same file.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/kit.py[R1495-1501]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/5/files#diff-c741f63d4fccb12bbfc566ee658f6a10d5d610c9e09e4a336f11292aaa5c1b37R1495-R1501) > >```diff >+ size = path.stat().st_size >+ if size > cap: >+ raise KitError( >+ f"hands kit apply: {path} is {size} bytes, over [files] kit_max_mb ({cap} bytes)" >+ ) >+ data = path.read_bytes() >+ answer = send({"name": path.name, "zip": base64.b64encode(data).decode("ascii")}) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>DEFAULT_KIT_MAX_MB is 20, while LINE_LIMIT = MAX_PROMPT_BYTES + MAX_PROMPT_BYTES // 4 is 12.5
>MiB. The client puts all kit bytes into a base64-encoded request, and call() uses
>_checked_request to reject requests over LINE_LIMIT. Because base64 expands the bytes by
>approximately 4/3, the effective zip ceiling is about 12.5 × 3/4 ≈ 9.4 MiB, below the configured kit
>cap.
>
> > [src/hands/config.py\[95-95\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/config.py/#L95-L95) > [src/hands/runner.py\[144-151\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/runner.py/#L144-L151) > [src/hands/cli.py\[1430-1460\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/cli.py/#L1430-L1460) > [src/hands/cli.py\[912-921\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/cli.py/#L912-L921) > [src/hands/kit.py\[1495-1501\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/kit.py/#L1495-L1501) > [src/hands/runner.py\[142-151\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/runner.py/#L142-L151) > [src/hands/cli.py\[1443-1459\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/src/hands/cli.py/#L1443-L1459) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`hands kit apply` accepts zips up to `kit_max_mb`, but base64 encoding can push a valid kit above the socket request limit before the daemon receives it. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/kit.py[1495-1501] >- src/hands/cli.py[914-921] >- src/hands/cli.py[1443-1459] >- src/hands/runner.py[142-151] > >## Recommended Fix >Either provide a bounded transfer mechanism that supports the configured kit limit, such as passing the zip path to the daemon for reading under `allowed_roots`, or make the advertised and enforced kit cap consistent with the encoded request limit. For the latter, use `min(kit_max_mb * MiB, LINE_LIMIT * 3 // 4 - envelope)` as the effective cap and have refusals name both limits. Test a kit above the current socket threshold but below the default kit limit. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
9. Quota capture can hang indefinitely ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>capture-quota-stop.sh runs hands and journalctl directly without a timeout wrapper. A hung
>daemon or journal query therefore leaves the foreground capture process waiting indefinitely instead
>of reaching its redaction and output steps.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh[R69-74]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/5/files#diff-8aaeceeb41390e763bbf25d16de0f7662c3cd93c4286e286af0ece466fe82359R69-R74) > >```diff >+ section "hands --project $project status" >+ run hands --project "$project" status >+ section "hands --project $project jobs -n 5" >+ run hands --project "$project" jobs -n 5 >+ section "hands --project $project pipeline" >+ run hands --project "$project" pipeline >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The compliance rule requires foreground subprocesses and shell commands to have explicit timeouts.
>The new capture script invokes hands status, hands jobs, hands pipeline, and journalctl
>without any timeout mechanism.
>
> > Rule 3263087: [Do not start background processes; run with explicit timeouts in foreground](https://app.qodo.ai/rules/3263087?state=active) > [scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh\[69-74\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh/#L69-L74) > [scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh\[130-135\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/fbe58a581216722428b701ab2e5b2f0346790fbc/scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh/#L130-L135) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The quota-capture script invokes external commands without explicit timeouts, so an unresponsive daemon or journal service can block the capture indefinitely. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh[69-74] >- scripts/capture-quota-stop.sh[130-135] > >## Recommended Fix >Wrap every external `hands` and `journalctl` invocation in an explicit timeout, preserve each command's failure output in the capture, and continue collecting later sections after a timeout. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies

- ## Actionable Suggestions
  - Concrete code fixes
  - Clear explanations
  - Prioritized feedback

- ## Security & Reliability Checks
  - Identifies risky patterns
  - Reduces attack surface area
